asks: when do I get a ping
a: The phone stays idle. The cloud checks the station about every 10 minutes. If your rule holds for the full hold time (default: 15 knots average for 20 minutes), you get a push. One gust is not enough — if it drops mid-hold, the hold resets. This is not a live poll on the phone. After a ping, signed-in users can mark Good or Meh.

q: How do I install / Add to Home Screen?
a: Open https://windsage.nimrod.bio/ . iPhone: Safari (not Chrome) → Share → Add to Home Screen, then open the icon and allow notifications — that is how lock-screen pings work best. Android: Chrome → menu → Add to Home screen / Install app. Or use Download in the app menu. Computer browser works too; allow site notifications if you want pings there.

q: How do I follow a station?
a: In the app: Add a station. Paste a Windguru number or URL (2259 is Freegull), an NDBC buoy id, Open-Meteo place, Synoptic/ICAO, or drop a map pin / address. Guest works on this device only. Sign in to keep the same list on another phone. Unfollow from the station screen.

q: What is the default wind rule?
a: Default: average wind ≥ 15 knots for 20 minutes. Simple presets: 12 / 15 / 18 / 20 kt average, or gusts 25 kt. Advanced (on the station): metric (avg, gust, waves, temp), hold minutes, max gust spread, direction window, max wave, max wind. Cloud wait is at least 1 minute; usual poll is about 10 minutes. The hold resets if the wind drops below the rule.

q: Does the phone drain battery / poll Windguru?
a: No phone polling. Background Windguru on the device is off. The cloud watches; the phone only receives the push. That is why it can stay idle, and why lock-screen readings are not a live 10-second tick.

In the app, Account → Continue with Google or Continue with Discord, or username & password (min 8 characters). Sign-in syncs follows across devices. This Discord helper is not the login screen. Join Discord is only the server invite — it does not log you into the app.

asks: do I need to sign in
a: Guest can follow on that device with no account. Sign in (Google, Discord, or password) to sync the list to another phone or computer. Guest phone and guest computer are two lists. Signing out clears the follow list on that device.

After an alert, signed-in users can mark Good or Meh. That is feedback on that ping (“was this useful?”), not a new wind rule. Guest cannot save it. Change the station rule in the app if the ping was the wrong kind of wind.
Wind is knots (kt), not mph. Waves in meters. Temperature in °C. Direction 0–360° (where the wind comes from). Roughly 15 kt ≈ 17 mph, 20 kt ≈ 23 mph — but you set the rule in knots in the app.

On the station screen, share the follow link. The other person opens it in Windsage (https://windsage.nimrod.bio/ or the Home Screen icon) and can follow the same target. Sharing does not force it onto their list.
Star a follow and move it up/down on Home so everyday spots stay at the top. Starring is list order only — each station still has its own alert rule.

Simple mode is on by default: fewer labels, Add a station, Put on home screen. Turn it off if you want full source names and extra rule fields (direction, max wave, gust spread). It does not change how pings work.

Map/Address: type a place or drop a pin. Windsage blends nearby stations by distance, accuracy, and rating inside a radius. Not one physical anemometer — treat it as wind in the area. You can open the pin in Google Maps. Use this when you have a place and no station number.

Open-Meteo is a weather model “now” at a lat,lon — not a cup anemometer on a mast. Windguru live / NDBC are real instruments when the station is live. Alerts on Open-Meteo still use your hold rule; they watch the model.

Windguru has forecast spots and live stations (instruments). Paste the URL or number. 2259 is Freegull (live). If live data is missing, the app may warn and can still use forecast for alerts — weaker than a live cup, but the follow still works.
NDBC/NOAA: US buoy or C-MAN id (example 41009). Wind plus waves when the buoy publishes them. Paste the id or the ndbc.noaa.gov station page URL. Real instruments on a schedule, not phone GPS.
Synoptic/MesoWest: airport ICAO or mesonet id, e.g. LLBG or KSLC. Needs the cloud token on the server; if it is not configured, pick Windguru/NDBC/map instead. This bot cannot turn that token on.

On the station (turn simple mode off if needed): average or gust, hold minutes, optional max gust spread (kt), direction window (from°–to°, 0–360), max wave (m), max wind (kt), temperature (°C). Comparisons are at least / at most. Cloud will not wait under 1 minute. Usual poll ~10 minutes.
